patients.summary: Retired construction foreman with COPD on home oxygen, metastatic non-small cell lung cancer under outside oncology, and prior DVT with post-thrombotic syndrome on warfarin. Joins in 2021, quits smoking in 2022, then has a run of postoperative and thrombotic emergencies (wound dehiscence, three pulmonary emboli, two hypercapnic COPD admissions) and a cardiac tamponade after his last practice visit. Outside records reach the practice unevenly.

documents.title: New patient scheduling call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Wife phoned on his behalf. Their old doctor retired and they heard about the membership model from a neighbor. He has lung cancer treated at an outside oncology office and is on oxygen at home, takes warfarin. Booked a 60 minute new patient slot 8/24 at 9:00. Asked her to bring all pill bottles and the oxygen company's name. Membership packet emailed. Records release form sent for the prior primary care office.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
66M here with his wife to establish. Previous PCP retired this summer.

PULM: COPD for years, on continuous O2 2 L by cannula since 2018; followed by an outside pulmonology group, who keep him on tiotropium daily, albuterol as needed and prednisone 5 mg daily as a maintenance dose. Walks the driveway and around the house with the portable concentrator. No hospital stays for his lungs in the past year by his account.

ONC: Lung cancer found Nov 2020 at an outside oncology group, already spread at diagnosis (non-small cell). Port placed then. Had chemo plus immunotherapy, now on pembrolizumab every 3 weeks through the port. Says the last scan was 'holding steady.' Tolerating it.

HEME: Leg clot 2019, has stayed on warfarin since, goal 2-3. Leg aches and feels heavy by evening, wears knee-high stockings most days (post-thrombotic). INRs had been done at the old office; would like us to take that over.

HTN on amlodipine 10.

TOBACCO: still smoking, about half a pack a day, down from much more; 40 pack-years. We talked plainly about cigarettes and oxygen in the same room. He knows. Not ready to set a date yet but willing to talk again.
Alcohol a drink or two a week. Retired construction foreman. Lives with wife.
FHx: father lung cancer, mother COPD, brother had a DVT.
NKDA.

Exam: thin, pleasant, nasal cannula in place, speaking full sentences. BP and SpO2 as charted on 2 L. Lungs: distant breath sounds, prolonged expiration, no crackles. Heart regular. Port right upper chest, clean. Legs: compression stockings on; no pitting today, mild brownish skin change at the ankles.

A/P
- COPD/chronic hypoxemic resp failure on home O2: continue regimen; pulm to keep managing.
- Metastatic NSCLC: per oncology; will request their notes.
- Hx DVT with PTS on warfarin: we will manage INR, nurse visit monthly to start. INR today.
- HTN: fine today, continue.
- Tobacco: revisit at each visit.
- Labs today, HCV and HIV once. Prior PCP records requested.
Back in ~3 months; INR check in 4 weeks.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Howard, everything from Tuesday came back fine: kidney and liver tests, blood counts, cholesterol all reasonable. INR was 2.4, right where we want it, so stay on 5 mg daily. Hep C and HIV screens negative. Our nurse will see you in about four weeks for the next INR.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Received by fax, 46 pages, covering 2015-2021 from his former primary care office. Highlights abstracted for PCP:
- Colonoscopy 2017: normal, no polyps.
- Left over to us: DVT treated 2019, warfarin indefinitely; INR log through June 2021, mostly 2-3.
- COPD, home oxygen ordered 2018.
- Hypertension on amlodipine 10 mg.
- Lung cancer diagnosed Nov 2020, care at oncology.
- Immunizations: influenza yearly; two COVID mRNA doses spring 2021; no pneumococcal conjugate on file; no Shingrix; last tetanus 2010.
Filed to media.

documents.title: Anticoagulation nurse visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In for INR. No bleeding, no bruising beyond usual, no missed doses, no new meds. Diet unchanged. Result in range, continue warfarin 5 mg every day. Next check in 4 weeks, booked.

documents.title: Oncology progress letter
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Outside oncology group — letter to new primary care physician, visit of 9/2/2021.

Mr. Finn is a 66-year-old man with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer diagnosed November 2020. Implanted port placed at diagnosis. He received four cycles of carboplatin, pemetrexed and pembrolizumab and has continued on pembrolizumab maintenance every three weeks. Restaging CT chest, abdomen and pelvis in August shows stable disease without new lesions. Tolerating treatment without immune-related toxicity; thyroid and liver tests normal on our labs.

Other: COPD on 2 L home oxygen, prednisone 5 mg daily, warfarin for prior DVT. Allergies: NKDA.

Plan: continue pembrolizumab every 3 weeks; port flushed with each infusion; CT every 3 months. We strongly support smoking cessation.

Thank you for sharing his care.

documents.title: INR and flu vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR drawn, in goal. No bleeding. Same dose. High-dose flu given left deltoid, tolerated, VIS given. Oncology aware he is getting flu shot (pt asked them last week, ok with immunotherapy). Next INR 4-5 wks, ties in with his 11/16 visit.

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Doing about the same. Breathing at baseline, using albuterol once or twice a day, more on cold mornings. Getting pembrolizumab q3wk, oncology says scans stable. Legs ache in the evenings, stockings help. Still smoking, ~8-10 a day. Says his wife wants him to quit more than he does. We spent a few minutes on what has worked for others; he'll think about patch vs. medication.

O: Vitals reviewed. Cannula on 2 L. Breath sounds diminished throughout, no wheeze today. RRR. No leg edema with stockings.

A/P:
1. COPD on home O2 - stable. Continue.
2. NSCLC - per onc.
3. Warfarin/hx DVT - INR today; monthly RN checks working well.
4. HTN - acceptable.
5. Tobacco - pre-contemplative-to-contemplative. Revisit in Feb.
6. Vaccines: PCV20 today, COVID booster today.
RTC 3 mo.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Came in today saying he is done with cigarettes. No single reason, just tired of it. Smoking 8-10/day. Prefers the patch, does not want a pill.

Breathing at baseline. No hemoptysis. Onc infusions continue without trouble.

Exam: vitals as charted, on 2 L. Lungs diminished, scattered end-expiratory wheeze that clears with cough. Heart RRR. Legs in stockings, no edema.

Plan:
- Nicotine patch 21 mg daily starting on his quit day (he picked 3/1). Plan 6 weeks at 21 then step down. Gum not needed per pt.
- Quitline number given. RN to call the week after.
- Again: no smoking anywhere near the oxygen.
- COPD, HTN, warfarin unchanged.

Stage IV NSCLC on pembrolizumab maintenance, now about 18 months from diagnosis. CT chest/abdomen/pelvis 5/5: stable disease, no new lesions. ECOG 1-2, limited mainly by his lungs. He has quit smoking since March, which we applaud. Labs today unremarkable including TSH.

Plan: continue pembrolizumab q3 weeks to complete two years of therapy, anticipated November 2022, then surveillance imaging. Meds and allergies (NKDA) reviewed.

Mood: PHQ-2 0.
Cognition: clock draw normal, 3/3 recall.
Tobacco: former since 3/2022. Alcohol 1-2/wk.
Advance care: has a health care proxy (wife); discussed goals briefly; wants full treatment for now and will talk with oncology about longer-term wishes.
Screening: colonoscopy 2017 normal; given metastatic cancer, will not pursue further colon screening. No AAA screen needed - he gets CT imaging every 3 months.
Vaccines: Tdap and Shingrix #1 today; #2 in 2-6 mo. Flu with next INR.
Exam: unchanged, lungs diminished, no edema.

Personalized plan printed for him.

Mr. Finn completed two years of pembrolizumab with his final dose 11/8/2022. CT chest/abdomen/pelvis 11/21: stable disease, no new lesions. No immune-related adverse effects over the course. Port to remain, flushed every 6-8 weeks at our infusion area.

Plan: observation with CT every 3 months and visit with each scan. Call with new cough change, weight loss, bone pain or neurologic symptoms.

documents.title: Office Visit - leg swelling
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
67M with COPD on 2 L O2, metastatic NSCLC under surveillance, prior DVT with post-thrombotic legs on warfarin, HTN on amlodipine 10.

CC: both ankles swollen x ~6 weeks. He read online that his blood pressure pill can do this and wants to know if that is it. Swelling is symmetric, softens overnight, worse after sitting. No orthopnea beyond his usual, no PND, breathing unchanged, no calf pain, no redness. Weight steady.

Exam: vitals as charted, SpO2 on 2 L at his usual. JVP not elevated. Lungs diminished, no crackles. Heart regular, no gallop. Both lower legs with symmetric 1-2+ pitting to mid-shin over the stocking line; calves soft, non-tender, no cords. Old hyperpigmentation at ankles unchanged.

A/P
1. Bilateral ankle edema, most consistent with dihydropyridine CCB effect at 10 mg on top of chronic venous changes. Symmetric, no heart failure signs, no one-sided findings to suggest a new clot (and he is therapeutic). Reduce amlodipine to 5 mg daily. Legs up when sitting, keep stockings. Recheck at post-op visit; home BP log in the meantime.
2. HTN: watching on the lower dose.
3. Surgery: he has gallbladder surgery booked with an outside general surgery group for 5/23. We do not have their consult note; requested. He needs warfarin hold instructions from the surgeon - asked him to have their office call us or send them.
4. COPD, NSCLC: no change.
RTC after surgery.

documents.title: Surgery and warfarin
documents.author: patient
documents.body: The surgeon's nurse called. They want me off the warfarin 5 days before May 23rd and they will tell me when to restart. Is that ok with you? Ankles a little better already on the half pill. BP at home 130s-140s over 80s. - Howard

documents.title: RE: Surgery and warfarin
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That plan is fine. Last dose would be the evening of May 17. Let the surgical team guide the restart, and come in for an INR about a week after you resume. Glad the swelling is easing and your home pressures look good.

documents.title: Anticoagulation nurse visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR in goal. Reviewed hold dates for May surgery, written on a card for him. Ankles visibly less puffy.

conditions.label: Disruption or dehiscence of closure of internal operation (surgical) wound of abdominal wall muscle or fascia, initial encounter

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: Indication: pain and bulge at recent upper abdominal incision, postoperative day 7. Technique: axial CT abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast. Findings: Postsurgical change of cholecystectomy. Defect in the fascial layer of the anterior abdominal wall at the incision with loops of small bowel protruding through it into the subcutaneous plane. No free intraperitoneal air beyond expected postoperative change. Liver, spleen, pancreas, kidneys and adrenals unremarkable. No hydronephrosis. Aorta normal caliber. Bowel proximal to the defect not dilated. Lung bases: emphysematous change.
reports.conclusion: Fascial dehiscence of the recent abdominal incision with protrusion of bowel loops through the defect.

documents.title: Emergency department record (received)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED, date of service 5/30/2023. Faxed to PCP 6/5.

HPI: 68-year-old man, one week out from an open cholecystectomy (started laparoscopic, converted), with COPD on 2 L home O2, metastatic lung cancer and prior DVT on warfarin (held for surgery). Was trying to lift a heavy box in the garage this morning when he felt something give way in his belly, followed at once by severe pain.

Allergies: NKDA. Meds: tiotropium, albuterol, warfarin (on hold), amlodipine 10 mg, prednisone 5 mg, O2 2 L.

Exam: afebrile; BP 130/85, HR 110, RR 22. Abdomen distended; bulge at the incision, tender, not reducible with gentle pressure; no redness or pus at the wound. Hypoactive bowel sounds.

Labs: WBC 11.0, Hgb 13.2, creatinine 1.0, BUN 18, lytes normal.
CT A/P: fascial defect with bowel loops through it.

Impression: deep fascial dehiscence of the operative wound.
Disposition: general surgery consulted in the ED, to OR this afternoon for closure; admitted to surgery. Operative and inpatient records to follow from the surgical service.

documents.title: Post-op follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen after the gallbladder operation and the return trip. Per pt and the ED fax: incision came apart at the fascia a week out when he lifted a box; closed in the OR the same day; home after 3 nights. Surgeon restarted warfarin on discharge. Lifting restriction 6 weeks, abdominal binder. Pain controlled with acetaminophen; no opioids left. Eating fine, BMs normal.

We have the ED record only - operative note, consult note and discharge summary not received. Second request faxed.

Exam: vitals as charted. Midline-upper abdominal incision healing, staples out, no erythema or drainage, binder on. Lungs diminished, unchanged. Legs: ankle swelling gone, stockings on.

A/P
1. S/p cholecystectomy c/b fascial dehiscence, repaired. Healing. Lifting limits reinforced.
2. Amlodipine edema - resolved on 5 mg. BP acceptable on the lower dose; keep 5 mg.
3. Warfarin resumed - INR today.
4. COPD, NSCLC - unchanged.
RTC 3 mo.

documents.title: Emergency department record (received)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED, date of service 9/17/2023 (received 9/25).

HPI: 68M, six days after an open radical prostatectomy at an outside urology group, discharged home 3 days ago and mostly in a chair since. Woke with sudden breathlessness and sharp chest pain on breathing in. Known DVT history; warfarin had been stopped for the operation and not yet restarted. COPD on 2 L at home; metastatic lung cancer.

Allergies: NKDA. Smoking: 40 pack-years, former.

Exam: T 37.2 C, BP 92/64, HR 115, RR 28, SpO2 88% on room air. Neck veins distended. Lungs clear. Loud P2.
ABG (room air): pH 7.47 / PaCO2 29 / PaO2 62.
CTPA: multiple bilateral segmental filling defects.

Impression: acute pulmonary embolism, postoperative.
Plan: heparin infusion, oxygen, admit to medicine; urology aware; warfarin to be resumed with overlap. Discharge summary to follow.

documents.title: Post-hospital visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here with wife. Honestly first we heard of the prostate operation was the ED fax yesterday - the urology group arranged it and the warfarin hold directly with him. He was home 3 days, then the PE on 9/17. Heparin then warfarin restarted in hospital; home 9/21 on warfarin 5 mg. No discharge summary or urology records here yet; requested both today.

Now: breathing back close to his usual, still tires on the stairs. No chest pain now. No hemoptysis. Catheter out; urology following.

Exam: vitals as charted; on 2 L, sats at his baseline. Lungs diminished, no rub. HR regular. Calves soft, no new asymmetry.

A/P
1. Acute PE, provoked (post-op, warfarin held) on background of cancer and prior DVT. Back on warfarin; INR today, then weekly x2.
2. S/p radical prostatectomy - per urology.
3. COPD on O2 - continue.
4. HTN - fine on amlodipine 5.
Discussed: any future surgery, we want to hear about it beforehand so the anticoagulation plan is coordinated.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary (received)
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital, admitted 3/19/2024, discharged 3/24/2024.

Diagnosis: acute exacerbation of COPD with acute hypercapnic respiratory failure.
Course: BiPAP overnight in step-down with improvement in mental alertness and CO2 by the next morning; weaned to his home 2 L by day 3. Nebulized bronchodilators, IV methylprednisolone 2 days then oral prednisone, doxycycline. Chest x-ray without pneumonia. INR therapeutic throughout on home warfarin.

Discharge medications: prednisone 40 mg daily x5 days then back to 5 mg daily; doxycycline 100 mg BID x5 days; continue tiotropium, albuterol, warfarin 5 mg, amlodipine 10 mg, O2 2 L continuous.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: PCP within 1 week; pulmonology.

documents.title: Post-discharge visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Reviewed discharge summary. Admitted 3/19-3/24 for COPD flare with high CO2, BiPAP overnight. On day 4 of the prednisone burst, finished doxycycline. Feels about 80% of baseline; walking room to room fine on 2 L.
Note the discharge list says amlodipine 10 - he takes 5, our list is correct; told him to keep taking 5.
Exam: vitals as charted. Scattered expiratory wheeze, moving air better than he describes. No accessory muscle use. No edema.
A/P
1. AECOPD w/ hypercapnic resp failure, resolving. Finish burst, back to prednisone 5. Pulmonology follow-up he has in April.
2. Antibiotic course with warfarin - INR today.
3. Reviewed when to call: more sleepiness, morning headaches, sats lower than usual.

Quarterly. Back at baseline since the March admission. Pulmonology saw him in April, no regimen change. Oncology scan in May stable per pt (letter pending).
Exam: vitals as charted. Lungs diminished, no wheeze. No edema.
A/P: stable on current list. Labs and INR today. Oxygen supplier recertification form signed. RTC 3 mo.

conditions.label: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease with acute exacerbation

reports.text: Portable AP chest. Lungs hyperinflated with flattened diaphragms. No focal consolidation, no pleural effusion, no pneumothorax. Heart size normal. Right chest port, catheter tip at the cavoatrial junction.

documents.title: Emergency department record (received late)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED, date of service 9/20/2024 (sent after second PCP request).

HPI: 69M, severe COPD on 2 L home O2 and metastatic lung cancer, six months after his last COPD exacerbation. Low-grade fever and tiredness for 3 days; in the past day much more short of breath and can't sleep lying down. Wife says the cough is worse, bringing up yellow-green phlegm.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: alert, worn out, using neck and shoulder muscles to breathe. RR 32, HR 112, T 37.8 C, SpO2 85% on room air. Expiratory wheezes both sides, reduced air entry at the bases. No JVD. No leg edema.
Arterial gas: abnormal acid-base status (see lab system).
CXR: hyperinflation, no focal infiltrate.

Impression: COPD exacerbation.
Plan: started on noninvasive positive pressure ventilation in the department; nebs, steroids, antibiotics; admitted to the ICU step-down.

medications.sig: Take 2 tablets (40 mg) by mouth daily for 5 days
Take 2 tablets on day 1, then 1 tablet daily on days 2-5

documents.title: Pharmacy call - new fills
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pharmacist called: filled hospital discharge Rxs yesterday for prednisone 40 mg x5 days and a 5-day azithromycin pack. Flagging azithro with warfarin. We had not known he was admitted. Called home - wife confirms he was in the hospital since 9/20 for his lungs, on the mask machine, home 9/25. Post-discharge visit booked 9/30 with INR.

conditions.label: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease with acute exacerbation

documents.title: Post-discharge visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Second COPD admission this year (9/20-9/25). No records from the hospital yet; history from pt and wife and the pharmacy fill. Fever and green sputum for a few days, then couldn't lie flat; put on the BiPAP-type mask in the ED, ICU step-down a couple of nights, no intubation. Home on prednisone 40 x5 and a Z-pack, both finished yesterday.
Today: tired, sleeping in the recliner still out of habit but can lie flatter. Cough improving, sputum clearer. No fever.
Exam: vitals as charted, on 2 L. Mild expiratory wheeze, no crackles. No edema. No JVD.
A/P
1. AECOPD, second this year - resolving. Back on prednisone 5. Asked pulmonology to see him sooner; ED record and discharge summary requested.
2. Azithro + warfarin - INR today.
3. Flu/COVID next nurse visit.

documents.title: INR and vaccines

documents.body:
AWV. Two COPD admissions this year; does the breathing exercises pulmonology showed him. Independent in ADLs, wife helps with IADLs and driving. No falls. PHQ-2 0. Cognition grossly intact.
Goals of care revisited: still wants hospital care including the mask machine; would not want a breathing tube long-term. Proxy (wife) aware. Will bring a written copy next time.
Vaccines up to date for this season. Lipids and INR today.
No change to meds.

conditions.label: Other pulmonary embolism with acute cor pulmonale
conditions.note: massive PE with hypotension and RV dysfunction; warfarin missed for a week

reports.text: Limited bedside study in the ICU. Right ventricle dilated with reduced free-wall motion. Left ventricle small, hyperdynamic. No pericardial effusion. Valves not assessed in detail.
Sinus tachycardia, rate about 120. Right bundle branch block. No acute ST elevation.
reports.conclusion: Sinus tachycardia with right bundle branch block.

documents.title: ICU / hospital discharge summary (received)
documents.author: pulmonary critical care
documents.body:
Regional hospital, Pulmonary & Critical Care. Admitted 3/30/2025, discharged 4/4/2025.

Presentation: 69-year-old man with COPD on home oxygen and prior PE who had not taken warfarin for the past week. Two hours of sudden breathlessness and pleuritic chest pain; lightheaded with a near-faint earlier that day. BP 85/50, HR 120, RR 28, SpO2 88% on room air. JVP raised; breath sounds reduced, no wheeze or crackles.
Troponin I, BNP and D-dimer all elevated. INR 1.2. Bedside echo: dilated, hypokinetic RV. ECG: sinus tachycardia, RBBB.

Diagnosis: massive pulmonary embolism.
Course: systemic alteplase given in the ICU with improvement in blood pressure within hours; heparin infusion after, bridged to warfarin. No bleeding complications. Weaned to home 2 L.

Discharge: warfarin 5 mg daily, INR 2.1 on day of discharge; continue tiotropium, albuterol, prednisone 5 mg, amlodipine 10 mg, O2 2 L. NKDA.
Follow-up: PCP INR within 4 days; adherence counseling given.

documents.title: Post-ICU visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Summary reviewed. Massive PE 3/30 after a week without warfarin; given clot-busting drug in the ICU, home 4/4 on warfarin 5 mg. He missed the February INR visit too. He does not give a clear reason for stopping the pills - 'just got off track.' Wife now setting out pills with his morning coffee and checking the box.
Now: winded with exertion more than before, no chest pain, no lightheadedness, no bleeding.
Exam: vitals as charted, on 2 L. Lungs diminished. HR regular. Calves soft.
A/P
1. Massive PE, recurrent VTE off anticoagulation. Warfarin 5 mg daily; INR today then weekly x3. Stressed not to skip doses again; pill box plan in place.
2. COPD on O2 - unchanged.
3. HTN - lower readings since discharge; keep amlodipine 5 for now.
RTC 2 mo.

Exam: vitals as charted. Lungs diminished, no wheeze. RRR. Stockings on; no edema.
A/P: COPD/home O2 stable. Recurrent VTE on warfarin - adherent. HTN fine. NSCLC surveillance per oncology. Labs today. RTC Aug/Sept, INR every 4 wks in between.

reports.text: Portable AP chest. Hyperinflated lungs. No consolidation to suggest pneumonia. No pneumothorax. No effusion. Right chest port in place.
Right lower extremity. Noncompressible proximal deep vein with echogenic intraluminal thrombus and absent augmentation. Calf veins limited by swelling. Left not examined.
reports.conclusion: Acute proximal deep vein thrombosis, right leg.

reports.study: CT angiogram chest, pulmonary embolism protocol
reports.text: CT pulmonary angiogram with IV contrast. Large filling defect straddling the bifurcation of the main pulmonary artery and extending into both main pulmonary arteries. Emphysema. No consolidation. No pericardial effusion. Port catheter tip at the cavoatrial junction.

procedures.procedure: Percutaneous insertion of inferior vena cava filter

documents.title: Admission history and physical (received)
documents.author: hematology oncology
documents.body:
Regional hospital, Hematology & Oncology service. Admission 9/20/2025. Sent to PCP 9/29.

HPI: 70-year-old man with COPD and metastatic NSCLC, six months after a massive PE. Recent right hip replacement at an outside orthopedic group; warfarin stopped for the operation and enoxaparin begun after it. For a week has had a productive cough with yellow sputum, which he put down to his COPD. Today sudden breathlessness and pleuritic chest pain, then vomited blood.
Meds: tiotropium, albuterol as needed, enoxaparin since surgery, warfarin (on hold), amlodipine 10 mg, prednisone 5 mg, O2 2 L. NKDA.

Exam: RR 28, SpO2 89% on room air, HR 110, BP 135/85. Right leg swollen and tender over the deep veins.
Labs: Hgb 7.8, Hct 23.4, platelets 255, INR 1.1, aPTT 30.
CXR: no pneumonia or pneumothorax. Right leg duplex: proximal DVT. CTPA: large saddle embolus.

Assessment: saddle pulmonary embolus with active GI bleeding; acute right proximal DVT.
Plan: hold all anticoagulation; transfuse; urgent GI endoscopy; IR for IVC filter; ICU monitoring. Resume anticoagulation when bleeding controlled. Discharge summary to follow.

medications.drug: omeprazole 40 MG Delayed Release Oral Capsule
medications.sig: Take 1 capsule by mouth daily before breakfast

documents.title: Post-hospital visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here with wife. We received only the admission H&P (9/29). From them and the H&P: right hip replaced in early September at an outside orthopedic group - we were not told beforehand; ortho stopped warfarin and gave him enoxaparin shots. 9/20 he coughed for a week, then sudden breathlessness and vomited blood; big clot across both lung arteries and a new right leg DVT. Given 2 units of blood, scoped (told the bleeding spot was treated, no report here), and had a filter put in the big vein. Warfarin restarted before he left 9/27 once the bleeding stopped; shots stopped. Started on omeprazole 40 daily. The hospital's anticoagulation clinic is now checking his INR and dosing - first check was 10/2.

Now: no further vomiting of blood, stools normal color. Short of breath at his baseline. Right leg still a bit swollen, less sore. Walking with a cane after the hip.

Exam: vitals as charted, on 2 L. Pale conjunctivae. Lungs diminished. RRR. Right leg mildly fuller than left, non-tender. Hip incision healed.

A/P
1. Saddle PE + right DVT with GI bleed, s/p IVC filter; back on warfarin via hospital anticoag clinic. We will stop our INR visits to avoid double dosing; asked them to fax results.
2. Anemia from bleed - Hgb 10.4 today, up from 7.8. Recheck next visit.
3. GI bleed - continue omeprazole; GI follow-up per hospital.
4. Hip replacement - ortho following; records requested.
5. Discharge summary and endoscopy report requested.

documents.title: Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: High-dose flu and this season's COVID given, firm pressure 2 min each site given warfarin. No bruising before he left. INR now managed by the hospital clinic; last value they gave him was in range.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Two months after the saddle PE and GI bleed. No more blood in vomit or stool. Breathing at his usual on 2 L. Off the cane around the house; ortho pleased with the hip per pt. Anticoag clinic adjusting warfarin, he says INRs in range; we have one faxed value from them only.
Discharge summary, endoscopy and ortho records still not received despite requests.

Exam: vitals as charted. Color better. Lungs diminished, no wheeze. Right leg minimally fuller than left, soft. Stockings on.

A/P
1. Recurrent VTE with saddle PE, IVC filter, on warfarin (hospital clinic).
2. Anemia after GI bleed, Hgb 11.6 today - improving.
3. COPD on home O2 - stable; prednisone 5, tiotropium.
4. HTN - fine on amlodipine 5.
5. NSCLC - oncology scan due December.
RTC 3 months; he will call to book after the holidays.

documents.title: Blood count
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Howard - your blood count is still climbing back (11.6), which is what we want after the bleeding. Keep taking the omeprazole. Please call before the end of February to set up your next visit. Happy Thanksgiving to you both.

documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy requests 90-day refills: tiotropium capsules, prednisone 5 mg, omeprazole 40 mg. Approved by PCP. Warfarin refills come from the anticoagulation clinic.

documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Outside oncology group, visit 12/16/2025 (received 2/17/2026).

Stage IV NSCLC on observation since 11/2022. CT 12/9: stable disease, no new lesions; IVC filter in place. September admission for saddle PE and GI bleeding noted; on warfarin, managed by the anticoagulation clinic. Port flushed. Continue CT every 3 months. NKDA.

reports.text: Urgent study. Pericardial effusion surrounding the heart with right atrial and right ventricular diastolic collapse and marked respiratory variation in mitral inflow. Left ventricle small and hyperdynamic. Inferior vena cava plethoric.

documents.title: Howard in the hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body: This is his wife writing on Howard's account. He collapsed at home Thursday morning and went by ambulance. They said fluid around his heart was squeezing it and drained it with a needle. He is in the cardiac unit, more awake now. I wanted you to know. They have not said when he can come home.

documents.title: RE: Howard in the hospital
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Thank you for letting us know, and we are sorry you are both going through this. Dr. has been told. Please call the office once he has a discharge date so we can set up a visit soon after, and ask the hospital to send us his summary.

documents.title: Cardiology discharge summary (received)
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Regional hospital, Cardiology. Admitted 4/2/2026, discharged 4/9/2026.

Presentation: 70-year-old man with metastatic lung cancer, severe COPD on home oxygen and recent massive PE and GI bleeding, brought in after collapsing at home; drowsy on arrival. BP 80/50, HR 118, RR 24. Distended neck veins, muffled heart sounds, weak thready pulse, cool extremities with slow capillary refill; systolic pressure fell 15 mm Hg on inspiration. Lungs clear. No leg edema.

Diagnoses: cardiac tamponade with cardiogenic shock.
Course: urgent echo showed a pericardial effusion with tamponade physiology. Emergent pericardiocentesis in the cath lab with prompt rise in blood pressure and improved alertness. Drain removed day 3. Monitored in CCU then telemetry.

Discharge medications (as listed): tiotropium, albuterol, warfarin 5 mg (INR goal 2-3), amlodipine 10 mg, prednisone 5 mg, O2 2 L continuous. NKDA.
Follow-up: cardiology 2 weeks with repeat echo; oncology; PCP.

documents.body: Request for amlodipine 5 mg 90-day. Approved x1 by PCP. Note to pt via pharmacy: due for a visit, please call to schedule.
